Purpose and exclusions

Create a common-body avatar with approved hair/palette/outfit choices and one of Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist or Warden. Class selection changes authored starting rules, not an invented race silhouette. The backend commits name, slot and appearance together.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create four DA_Class_* definitions with display text, common BodyId=body.common and separate class IDs; abilities can be unassigned until the combat phases.
  2. Place Preview_Avatar in L_FrontEnd with collision disabled, no replication, no PlayerState and no authoritative component; use the art resolver in preview mode.
  3. Build WBP_CharacterCreate with a step heading, previous/next controls, class description, name field and preview rotation disabled. Facing preview buttons are discrete direction choices, not a world camera rotation option.
  4. In WBP_CharacterSelect bind Create, EnterWorld, Delete and Restore to URPGCharacterRoster requests. Delete requires typing the displayed character name and explains the recovery policy.
  5. Reopen BP_RPGPlayerController: after admission completes, remove preview widgets, clear pending input and request the initial zone connection; do not manually spawn an extra gameplay character.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect
CreateCharacter(CommandId, SlotIndex, Name, ClassId, AppearanceChoices) -> CharacterSummary|NameUnavailable|InvalidAppearanceNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
SelectCharacter(CharacterId) -> AdmissionTicket|AlreadyOnline|ForbiddenNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
RequestDeleteCharacter(CommandId, CharacterId, TypedName) -> SoftDeleted|BusyNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
RestoreCharacter(CommandId, CharacterId) -> Restored|RecoveryExpired|NameConflictNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Character slots, creation, selection and recovery. Rule owner: URPGCharacterRoster. This asset’s role is Create a common-body avatar with approved hair/palette/outfit choices and one of Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist or Warden. Class selection changes authored starting rules, not an invented race silhouette. The backend commits name, slot and appearance together.

  1. Appearance controls modify only the preview actor. Validate that each selection exists in the client catalog but repeat validation in the backend.
  2. After confirmation, send the command ID, chosen slot and catalog identifiers; generate no authoritative character UUID in UMG.
  3. Backend authenticates AccountId, checks slot/name uniqueness, class availability and appearance allowlists, and inserts character, starting progression, appearance and command receipt in one transaction.
  4. Starter item grants, when enabled in Phase 09, use a unique character-creation entitlement rather than rerunning grants on every login.
  5. Refresh the slot list from the committed summary and resolve preview visuals with the same appearance resolver used by remote avatars.
  6. After disconnect, list/select the existing CharacterId; target zone loads the durable appearance and replicates only safe appearance IDs.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_FrontEnd / Preview_Avatar / Account_A. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Two simultaneous identical normalized names -> one Created, one NameUnavailable.
Same CommandId with same payload -> same CharacterId; different payload -> IdempotencyConflict.
Hair from unsupported page/body -> InvalidAppearance or a documented cosmetic fallback; no fabricated compatible art.
Delete while character lease is active -> Busy; never remove inventory rows underneath a live session.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
